prompt:
I need the front end for Eastside Ledger Desk. A writing desk for one-person hobby newsletters that lets the writer hand an AI assistant a reporting task and then check every claim it produces against the source documents before publishing.

Who's using it: Doug Ferreira, a retired high-school civics teacher. On his own time he writes a free weekly email newsletter about his town's local government, which goes to 340 neighbors. He's careful about accuracy and suspicious of anything he can't trace to a document.

What they're doing right now: It's Wednesday night, and the issue goes out Thursday at 7am. Earlier he asked the assistant: "Read the three council and planning meeting minutes from this week plus the two city press releases, and draft a 'What Council Did' section with plain-language items under 80 words each." The assistant has finished. It produced 7 items, rated 2 of them low-confidence, and noted that it couldn't locate a source for a quote it attributed to Councilmember Okafor. Doug needs to go through each item: confirm what it's based on, reject or rewrite the shaky ones, and decide whether to tell the assistant to redo item 5 using only the planning minutes.

What's in the system at this point: The task holds the original instruction text and 5 source documents: council minutes for Nov 10 (14 pages), a special session on Nov 12 (4 pages), planning commission minutes for Nov 13 (9 pages), and two press releases (on the leaf-pickup schedule and a water main replacement). The assistant's work log has 11 steps with timestamps, including "skipped pages 6–8 of council minutes: scanned image, text unreadable." There are 7 draft items totaling 512 words. Each claim is linked to a document and page; 3 claims have no link. Confidence is high for 5 items and low for 2: item 3 (a vote count of 4–3 vs. 5–2) and item 5 (rezoning on Alder St). Doug's past issues show a 380-word house limit for this section.

Build it as a working web app, opened in the state that person would see at that moment. No backend: use realistic mock data (no lorem ipsum, no placeholder names), and make the interactive parts actually work client-side.

Use whatever framework and tooling you like. When you're done there must be a static production build in ./out with ./out/index.html as the entry point. It will be served from the root of a plain static file server (no rewrites, no server code) and viewed in a desktop browser at 1440×900.
